chapter: Learning drums and Roy Eldridge's band
title: Pittsburgh clubs, jamming and Little Louis
summary: Joining Roy in a Pittsburgh cabaret; Pittsburgh was a tough town for visiting musicians, with trumpeter Little Louis and Roy cutting visitors.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Oh, very well. Very well. Wonderful arranger. And I joined the band, we were playing in a cabaret in Pittsburgh.
Now what year are you in?
Now I'm in around '32.
Oh. So -- you are in '32. Had you ever heard Roy blow?
Oh, yeah. He used to jam. I used to hear him jamming in all the clubs around home.
Well, what clubs did you used to go to to jam?
Well, let me see, there was The Brown Derby.
Yeah.
There was a fellow, Gus Greenlee's club. What was the name of that club?
Oh, it doesn't matter, Kenny.
But we had quite a few clubs around home at that time.
It was jumping.
Oh, yeah. Pittsburgh was the town.
Yeah.
And --
Lots of people didn't know that.

Oh, boy. Any musician, they were kind of afraid to come to Pittsburgh, because they could find their -- meet their match there, you know. I don't care what instrument you played, we were always running around and knock on the door of some trumpet player. And Little Louis, we used to call him, say, "Hey, Little Louis, there's a trumpet player from Fletcher Henderson's band who thinks he can blow." And Louis said, "Oh, yeah?" And he would take his horn right out, no case or nothing, just take his horn and run down to the cabaret and listen, and then start blowing.
Would he really blow?
Oh, Lord.
What was his last name?
I don't know. I don't remember what Louis's name was. We used to call him Little Louis. Yeah, he
was the one we would always get when we had a tough trumpet player from New York or somewhere. We'd call Louis and sometimes Roy would take over, you know.
